input: Create a shared family calendar everyone can edit

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of family members, their ages, and tech comfort levels determine how simple or guided the setup needs to be, and whether parental controls are needed.
Knowing what types of events to include (appointments, school, chores, holidays, etc.) shapes how the calendar should be structured and categorized.
The platform choice (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Cozi, etc.) depends on what devices the family already uses, and determines the entire technical setup path.
Whether the family wants a free solution or is open to a paid app significantly narrows the tool options.
Whether this calendar needs to sync with existing personal calendars affects the integration steps required.
Whether each person should see everything or have their own color-coded or permission-limited view changes how the calendar is organized and shared.
Understanding what has failed or felt frustrating before (e.g., people not updating it, hard to read at a glance) defines what 'done well' actually means for this family.

gold.taskTitle: Create a shared editable family calendar
gold.taskDescription: Set up a shared calendar that all family members can access and edit to coordinate schedules and events.

questions.title: How many people need access, and what are their ages?
questions.description: Knowing the size of the family and whether children are involved determines complexity, permission needs, and how beginner-friendly the setup must be.

questions.title: What types of events will this calendar track?
questions.description: Identify whether this covers appointments, school schedules, chores, holidays, travel, or everything — this shapes how the calendar is structured and labelled.

questions.title: What devices does your family mainly use — Apple, Android, or mixed?
questions.description: Device ecosystem is the single biggest factor in which calendar platform will work seamlessly for everyone without friction.

questions.title: Are you open to a paid app, or does it need to be free?
questions.description: Budget constraint directly filters the tool options, since dedicated family apps like Cozi or TimeTree have paid tiers while Google Calendar is free.

questions.title: Does it need to sync with anyone's existing personal calendar?
questions.description: If family members already use work or school calendars, integration requirements will add steps and affect which platform is chosen.

questions.title: Should everyone see all events, or have their own personal view?
questions.description: This determines whether one shared calendar is enough or whether individual color-coded sub-calendars with selective visibility need to be configured.

questions.title: Has a shared calendar been tried before, and what went wrong?
questions.description: Past failures (e.g., people not updating it, hard to read on mobile) reveal what the new setup must specifically solve to count as a success.
